content.text:
The best map I found scores mAP 0.2295, up from the 0.2203 baseline. I'm stopping here with 7 of 15 evaluation calls used, since the last several changes gained almost nothing.

**Best prompt map (mAP 0.2295):**
- **car:** "car", "van", "sedan", "suv"
- **truck:** "truck", "lorry"
- **pedestrian:** "pedestrian", "person"
- **cyclist:** "bike rider"
- **tram:** "tram"

**Per-class AP for this map:**

| Class | AP | AP50 |
|---|---|---|
| car | 0.380 | 0.751 |
| truck | 0.316 | 0.574 |
| pedestrian | 0.204 | 0.489 |
| cyclist | 0.012 | 0.064 |
| tram | 0.236 | 0.533 |

**What the calls showed:**
- **Car:** "sedan" and "suv" each had high precision (31 and 93 correct, only 2 and 7 false positives), and they raised car AP from 0.373 to 0.380.
- **Truck:** "lorry" had good precision (9 correct, 6 false positives). "delivery truck" added false positives and was dropped.
- **Pedestrian:** "person" alongside "pedestrian" helped slightly. "pedestrian on sidewalk" was poor and was dropped.
- **Cyclist:** This is the main weakness. AP stayed near 0.012 across every wording I tried, including "bicycle", "bike", "person on bike", "man on bicycle" and "bicycle rider". Cyclist AP50 is only about 0.06, so the detector is finding the bike or rider but not boxes that match the combined rider-plus-bicycle ground truth. Text wording alone did not fix this.
- **Tram:** "streetcar" hurt tram precision, and "light rail" and "tram on rails" did not improve AP. The plain word "tram" was best.

I'll keep going with the next probe. The best map so far is the 0.2295 set. Car synonyms that behaved like "sedan" and "suv" (high precision) are a reasonable next target, so I'm adding "minivan", "hatchback" and "station wagon".
